In 1814, a wave of beer flooded the streets of London.
At the Horse Shoe Brewery, a giant wooden vat held over half a million litres of beer.
It was held together by huge iron rings.
On October the seventeenth, one of the rings slipped.
An hour later, the whole vat burst.
The blast smashed open the other vats too.
More than a million litres of beer broke through the brewery wall.
A wave up to fifteen feet high rushed into the slum of St Giles.
It crashed into houses and flooded the cellars. Eight people died.
Some people scooped up the beer in pots and pans.
In court, the judge called it an act of God. Nobody was blamed.
And the brewery even got its beer tax refunded.
